title: Institutional vs ad-hoc arbitration - what clients should actually choose
p1:
Many businesses choose arbitration thinking every process is the same. But one small decision at the beginning can completely change how smooth, costly, and predictable the dispute process becomes.

The real question is not "Is arbitration better?" It is: should you choose institutional or ad-hoc arbitration?
p2:
A common misconception is that ad-hoc arbitration is always cheaper and institutional arbitration is always better. The reality is more balanced.

In ad-hoc arbitration, the parties manage the process themselves, including choosing rules and handling administration. This can offer flexibility, but disagreements about procedure can create delays.

Institutional arbitration involves an arbitration organization that provides rules, support, and administrative assistance. Many clients do not realize that this structure can reduce confusion when disputes become complex.
p3:
The practical takeaway: the right choice depends on the dispute, the relationship between parties, the amount involved, and how much process support is needed. A simple dispute between experienced parties may work well with ad-hoc arbitration, while larger commercial matters may benefit from institutional support.

Choosing the arbitration method is not a formality. It is part of risk planning.
conclusion: If you were drafting a business contract today, would you prefer institutional arbitration or ad-hoc arbitration, and why?
